summary.problem: When the floating sidebar was open, the top-right toolbar buttons (including the hamburger menu trigger) rendered above the sidebar at z-index 100, obscuring it. Tapping the hamburger button also had no effect on the sidebar, because the trigger button carried a `data-prevent-outside-click` attribute that silenced every panel's outside-click handler globally — so the sidebar never heard the tap.
summary.solution: Raise the sidebar's z-index above the toolbar. Remove the global suppress attribute from the trigger, replacing it with a targeted container-level check inside the menu's own outside-click handler, so the menu still ignores clicks on its own trigger while the sidebar's handler now correctly fires.

plain.title: Sidebar closes when you tap the main menu button
plain.problem: When the sidebar was open, toolbar buttons were drawn on top of it, and tapping the hamburger button never closed the sidebar because a global suppress flag silenced the close signal.
plain.fix: The sidebar now draws above all toolbar buttons, and tapping the hamburger correctly closes the sidebar before the menu opens.

steps.title: Buttons appear above the sidebar, and clicking them doesn't close it
steps.headline: Toolbar buttons sit on top of the open sidebar
steps.say: When the sidebar is open, buttons in the top-right corner overlap it, and tapping the hamburger button does not close the sidebar.
steps.narration: The editor has a floating sidebar on the right edge showing the element library. When the sidebar is open, all top-right toolbar buttons — including the hamburger icon — are drawn on top of it, obscuring part of the panel. Clicking those buttons also has no effect on the sidebar, so on mobile both the sidebar and the main menu end up open simultaneously.

Tapping the menu button does not close the sidebar

beats.heading: How it works now
beats.text: The sidebar uses `--zIndex-ui-library: 80`. The `.App-top-bar`, which holds all top-right toolbar buttons, uses `--zIndex-ui-top: 100`. Both share a stacking context, so 100 > 80 means the toolbar always renders on top.

lines.annotation: Sidebar z-index — below --zIndex-ui-top (100), so toolbar renders above it.
App-top-bar and all toolbar buttons use this value, placing them above the sidebar.

sources.ref: move sidebar above top layer UI so buttons aren't above the sidebar when open

steps.title: Sidebar z-index raised above the top-right toolbar
steps.headline: Sidebar z-index leapfrogs the toolbar buttons
steps.say: One number change gives the sidebar a higher stacking order than all toolbar UI, so buttons no longer overlap the panel.
steps.check: Open the sidebar, then check that top-right buttons (library trigger, collaborator avatars) appear behind the sidebar panel, not in front of it.
steps.narration: The simplest part of the fix: raise `--zIndex-ui-library` from 80 to 120, which puts it above `--zIndex-ui-top` at 100. The sidebar now draws in front of every top-right toolbar button. The declaration is also moved later in the stylesheet list to reflect the new order.

beats.heading: What we change
beats.text: `--zIndex-ui-library` moves from 80 (below `--zIndex-ui-top: 100`) to 120 (above it). The declaration is repositioned in the variable list to match.

lines.annotation: 120 > 100: the sidebar now renders above the top-right toolbar in the same stacking context.

steps.title: The hamburger tap was shielded from the sidebar's outside-click detector
steps.headline: The hamburger button was invisible to the sidebar's close logic
steps.say: The sidebar listens for taps outside itself to close. But the hamburger button told that listener to ignore it — so tapping the button never closed the sidebar.
steps.narration: The sidebar closes itself on outside taps via the shared `useOutsideClick` hook. That hook has a blanket escape hatch: if the tapped element carries `data-prevent-outside-click` anywhere in its ancestor chain, the hook returns early. The dropdown trigger button — the hamburger — carried exactly that attribute, so the sidebar's close handler was never called when the user tapped it.

beats.heading: How it works now
beats.text: Any click whose target has `data-prevent-outside-click` in its ancestor chain is treated as an inside click for every registered `useOutsideClick` handler, including the sidebar's.

lines.text: // clicking on a container that ignores outside clicks

lines.annotation: This check is global — it silences every panel's outside-click handler, not just the dropdown's own.
This attribute causes the sidebar (and every other panel) to ignore pointer-down events on the hamburger button.

beats.heading: What breaks
beats.text: When the user taps the hamburger while the sidebar is open, `useOutsideClick` skips the sidebar's `closeLibrary` callback. The sidebar stays open.

steps.title: Simply removing the attribute would break the menu's own toggle behaviour
steps.headline: Why the flag could not simply be deleted
steps.say: Without the flag, tapping the menu button while the menu is open counts as a tap outside the menu, so it closes and the same click opens it again — the button seems to do nothing. That is why the next steps protect the menu first, and only then remove the flag.
steps.narration: The dropdown menu content has its own `useOutsideClick` registration. When the menu is open and the user taps the trigger, the content's handler fires because the trigger is outside the menu panel's ref. Without the global suppress attribute, `onClickOutside` fires and closes the menu — on the same pointer-down that the button's own click handler will use to toggle the menu open. The result is a toggle that immediately undoes itself. The attribute existed to prevent this.

beats.heading: The menu’s own close-on-outside-tap
beats.text: The menu panel closes on any tap outside its own box. The menu button is outside that box, so without the flag a tap on the button would close the menu.

lines.annotation: The button is not inside menuRef, so a tap on it counts as “outside”.

beats.heading: Why we can't simply remove the attribute
beats.text: With the attribute gone, a pointer-down on the trigger fires both the button's `onClick` (open) and `DropdownMenuContent`'s `useOutsideClick` (close) in the same gesture. The menu would flash open and close instantly.

traces.label: useOutsideClick (MenuContent fires — trigger is outside panel ref)

notes: The order of pointer-down vs click and the net state is inferred from how React event batching works. The exact sequencing has not been run.

sources.ref: DropdownMenuContent useOutsideClick + trigger button click ordering

steps.title: Wrap trigger and content together so the menu recognises its own trigger
steps.headline: Trigger and menu panel get a shared wrapper
steps.say: Rather than a global suppress flag, the trigger and the open panel are grouped in a shared container, so only the menu itself knows to ignore clicks on its own button.
steps.check: Open the main menu, then click the hamburger button again. The menu should close — not close and immediately reopen.
steps.narration: The fix wraps the trigger button and the open menu panel in a single div with the class `dropdown-menu-container`, using `display: contents` so there is no layout impact. The menu's outside-click callback can now walk the DOM from its panel to that container and check whether the tap was inside it. If yes — meaning the user tapped the trigger — the menu's own `onClickOutside` is not called, and the button's click handler manages open state alone. Crucially, the sidebar's `useOutsideClick` has no such exception, so it still fires and closes the sidebar.

beats.heading: What we change in DropdownMenu
beats.text: The fragment `<>…</>` is replaced with `<div className="dropdown-menu-container" style={{ display: 'contents' }}>`, grouping trigger and content without affecting layout.

lines.text: // remove this div from box layout

lines.annotation: `display: contents` means this div is a pure DOM grouping node — no box is generated, so flex/grid parents don't see it.

steps.title: Menu content checks its container before calling onClickOutside
steps.headline: Menu only closes for clicks truly outside its container
steps.say: The menu panel now walks up to its container and asks if the tap landed inside it — including on the trigger button — before deciding to close.
steps.check: While the menu is open, clicking the trigger button should close the menu (button's own handler fires); clicking anywhere else outside should also close it.
steps.narration: The `DropdownMenuContent` now receives the click event, walks up to the nearest `dropdown-menu-container` ancestor, and checks whether that container contains the click target. If it does — that is, if the tap was on the trigger — `onClickOutside` is not called. The button's own `onClick` toggle handler manages the state. If the tap is outside the container, `onClickOutside` fires as before. This replaces the global suppress attribute with a scoped, targeted check.

beats.heading: How it worked before
beats.text: The callback passed to `useOutsideClick` took no arguments and called `onClickOutside` unconditionally.

lines.annotation: No event parameter — the handler can't inspect what was clicked.

beats.heading: What we change
beats.text: The callback receives the event, walks to the container, and guards `onClickOutside` behind a `contains` check.

lines.text: // prevents closing if clicking on the trigger button

lines.annotation: If the click target is inside the container (e.g., the trigger), the `!` makes this false and `onClickOutside` is skipped. This replaces the global attribute check.

steps.title: The suppress-click attribute is removed from the trigger button
steps.headline: Tap the menu button to close the sidebar
steps.say: With the targeted container check protecting the menu, the global suppress flag on the trigger button is removed. The sidebar's close handler now fires when the button is tapped.
steps.check: Open the sidebar, then tap the hamburger trigger. The sidebar should close and the main menu should open — not both remain visible.
steps.narration: With the menu now guarding itself via the container check, the global `data-prevent-outside-click` attribute on the trigger is no longer needed. Removing it means the sidebar's `useOutsideClick` handler finally fires when the user taps the hamburger. The sequence is: pointer-down fires, the sidebar's handler runs and calls `closeLibrary`, then the button's click event fires and opens the main menu.

beats.heading: What we change
beats.text: One attribute removed from the trigger button — the global suppress is gone.

lines.annotation: Removing this lets the sidebar's useOutsideClick handler fire when the trigger is tapped, closing the sidebar.

steps.title: Hook callback type narrowed to allow accessing event.target
steps.headline: A supporting type change for the new check
steps.narration: The outside-click hook's callback previously typed the event as a plain `Event`, which TypeScript does not allow calling `.closest` on. The new container check in `DropdownMenuContent` needs `event.target`, so the callback type is narrowed to `Event & { target: T }`.

beats.heading: What we change
beats.text: The callback signature adds `{ target: T }` to the event type so callers can use `event.target` safely.

openQuestions.question: The class `dropdown-menu-container` is also used on the inner Island and Stack.Col elements inside `DropdownMenuContent`. Could `menuRef.current.closest('.dropdown-menu-container')` find one of those inner elements instead of the new outer wrapper, making the trigger-click guard silently fail?
openQuestions.why: In DropdownMenuContent.tsx the Island (line 87) and Stack.Col (line 84) both carry `className='dropdown-menu-container'`. Since `.closest()` walks upward from `menuRef.current`, it would hit the outer wrapper div first — but this depends on the DOM structure, and a future change moving the inner class name could break the guard silently.
openQuestions.short: Does `.closest` find an inner element instead of the outer wrapper?

openQuestions.question: Other components that use `DropdownMenu.Trigger` (e.g. the extra-tools menu in `MobileToolBar`) previously inherited the `data-prevent-outside-click` protection. Do any of them now break because tapping their trigger incorrectly fires outside-click handlers on other open panels?
openQuestions.why: The attribute was removed globally from `DropdownMenuTrigger`, so every `DropdownMenu` instance loses the suppress attribute — not just the main menu.
openQuestions.short: Do other dropdown triggers break without the suppress attribute?

openQuestions.question: The sidebar z-index is now 120, above `--zIndex-ui-top: 100` and the hardcoded `z-index: 100` on `layer-ui__wrapper__footer-right`. Are there panels or buttons that legitimately need to appear above the sidebar?
openQuestions.why: `layer-ui__wrapper__footer-right` uses a hardcoded z-index of 100, and other UI like context menus (90) and style popups (100) are now all below the sidebar — are those interactions correct?
openQuestions.short: Does anything at z-index 100 need to appear above the sidebar?

- move sidebar above top layer UI (especially top-right) so that buttons aren't above the sidebar when open
- close sidebar (when not docked) when opening main menu. This is necessary otherwise the previous change would make the main menu below the sidebar on mobile.
